evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leadership supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace powers, and appointment/dismissal authority over key state posts; Article 113 says the president is highest official only outside matters directly concerned with the Leadership.
evidence.title: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran
evidence.publisher: University of Minnesota Human Rights Library
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leadership supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace powers, and appointment/dismissal authority over key state posts; Article 113 says the president is highest official only outside matters directly concerned with the Leadership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text with stable formal allocations of authority and limits.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly defines the office held by Ali Khamenei in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The text shows formal powers, not whether Khamenei exercised them prudently in 2022.
The president retains ordinary executive responsibility outside Leadership matters.

evidence.claim: Khamenei told officials not to make economic development conditional on sanctions relief and said the country should be run so sanctions do not hurt it.
evidence.title: Leader: Iran's economy should not be tied to US sanctions, country must become impervious to bans
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei told officials not to make economic development conditional on sanctions relief and said the country should be run so sanctions do not hurt it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: State-affiliated outlet quoting Khamenei's televised New Year speech and linking it to khamenei.ir.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and close to the nuclear negotiations period.
contrary_evidence: This is economic strategy rather than nuclear safety policy.
Sanctions resilience can be read as hardline posture rather than risk reduction.

evidence.claim: Higher oil and tax revenues improved the fiscal deficit ratio, but inflation was eroding low-income welfare; the report projected a 4.4 percent fiscal deficit for 2022-24 and recommended infrastructure investment, a better business environment, and well-targeted social safety transfers.
evidence.title: Iran Economic Monitor, Spring 2022: Managing Economic Uncertainties
evidence.excerpt: Higher oil and tax revenues improved the fiscal deficit ratio, but inflation was eroding low-income welfare; the report projected a 4.4 percent fiscal deficit for 2022-24 and recommended infrastructure investment, a better business environment, and well-targeted social safety transfers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank country-monitor summary; the page is a high-quality synthesis but the snippet is shorter than a full report excerpt.
evidence.period_fit: Published during 2022 and explicitly about the 2021/22 and 2022-24 outlook.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level context, not a direct Khamenei policy record; useful for the welfare and implementation environment under his rule.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes higher oil and tax revenues, so it is not a pure deterioration story.

evidence.claim: The paper finds that fiscal deficits, currency depreciation, and sanctions drive inflation in Iran, and recommends gradual deficit reduction, stronger central-bank autonomy and accountability, and more private-sector competition, rule of law, and banking reform.
evidence.title: Determinants of Inflation in Iran and Policies to Curb It
evidence.excerpt: The paper finds that fiscal deficits, currency depreciation, and sanctions drive inflation in Iran, and recommends gradual deficit reduction, stronger central-bank autonomy and accountability, and more private-sector competition, rule of law, and banking reform.
evidence.source_locator: Abstract / summary and short-term priorities section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF working paper on Iran-specific inflation drivers and policy options; it is research rather than a policy directive, but the diagnosis is explicit and contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Uses data through 2021 and was published in 2022, making it a strong near-period analytical source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect policy context; it identifies the policy environment Khamenei controlled, but not a single ruler-order by itself.
contrary_evidence: The paper is explanatory research, not a finding that Khamenei personally adopted the recommended reforms.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that ordinary Iranians were facing a severe cost-of-living squeeze while official targets still called for 8 percent growth; the piece also described worsening economic hardship amid sanctions and mismanagement.
evidence.title: Iran's cost-of-living squeeze belies push for economic self-reliance
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that ordinary Iranians were facing a severe cost-of-living squeeze while official targets still called for 8 percent growth; the piece also described worsening economic hardship amid sanctions and mismanagement.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and quoted witness accounts
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on public economic conditions; it is not official data, but it is independent and close to the events.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The article reflects the regime's economic stance and reported public hardship, but it does not by itself isolate Khamenei's personal choice from the broader Raisi government.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes that the state still publicly targeted 8 percent growth, so it shows aspiration as well as hardship.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Iran's central bank governor partly blamed anti-government unrest and U.S. sanctions for the rial's record lows and that the currency had lost nearly 20 percent of its value since the protests began.
evidence.title: Iran central bank governor blames protests for currency's fall
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Iran's central bank governor partly blamed anti-government unrest and U.S. sanctions for the rial's record lows and that the currency had lost nearly 20 percent of its value since the protests began.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Reuters reporting with specific market data and contemporaneous attribution from the central bank governor.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The currency shock reflects both policy and external pressure; the report does not isolate Khamenei's personal decision, but it is relevant to regime-level economic management.
contrary_evidence: Sanctions and protest unrest are real confounders, so the currency fall cannot be attributed to domestic policy alone.

evidence.claim: The Persian-language reproduction of Khamenei's seventh development-plan guidelines sets economic progress with justice as the main goal, targets an average 8 percent growth rate, calls for single-digit inflation over five years, and directs liquidity and bank credit toward productive activities rather than non-productive ones.
evidence.title: سیاست‌های کلی برنامه پنج ساله هفتم
evidence.excerpt: The Persian-language reproduction of Khamenei's seventh development-plan guidelines sets economic progress with justice as the main goal, targets an average 8 percent growth rate, calls for single-digit inflation over five years, and directs liquidity and bank credit toward productive activities rather than non-productive ones.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language reproduction of the decree's wording; the host site is secondary, but the text is specific and clearly attributed to the Supreme Leader's guidelines.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to September 2022 and explicitly about the next five-year plan.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Supreme Leader guideline, though hosted on a secondary Persian site rather than the original office domain.
contrary_evidence: This is a planning decree, not proof that the targets were met in practice.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on Khamenei's own 2022 command-and-control or safety governance is thin.
Risk-reduction evidence is mostly procedural rather than demonstrated durable restraint.
Proxy and drone-transfer evidence is strong on state conduct but weak on direct Khamenei ordering.
The diplomatic track is shown as a process, not a clearly completed peace or de-escalation achievement.
Direct personal orders are still sparse, so command-chain attribution remains system-level in places.
There was no 2022 election contestation event, so practice evidence for contestability is indirect.
Several strongest items are protest-repression evidence that overlaps heavily with Chapter 3B.
Direct Khamenei-attributed economic implementation evidence is thin relative to macro context.
Household and regional distribution effects are better described than attributed.
Direct ruler-attributed welfare decisions remain thin compared with UN/agency delivery material.
The package is stronger on refugees, children, and UN-supported programs than on the whole-population welfare picture.
Direct 2022 evidence on Khamenei's own assets, disclosures, gifts, or self-dealing remains absent.
Admissions of error, corrective behavior, and independent scrutiny are thin.
The plan-to-implementation chain is still incomplete.
Outcome evidence exists, but durable goal progress is only partly established and is confounded by sanctions, protests, and macro stress.
